subject: Ellis: Questions on hosted API data residency & purge controls
messages:
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@ellis.co>

Cc: Ellis & Co Procurement <procurement@ellis.co>

Subject: Questions on hosted API data residency & purge controls

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the quick demo last week. Our security team reviewed the hosted API notes and attached questionnaire (see attached PDF) and came back with a short set of clarifying questions around residency, retention windows, and deletion guarantees for the hosted offering. They asked that we capture these in writing for our procurement packet. Can you confirm the following for our Ellis production tenancy (US region):

1) Where is customer data stored at rest for the hosted API? Is it limited to a single region or replicated across regions?
2) What retention windows are configurable per tenant? Can we set a 30-day max for conversational logs and ensure token-level audit logs are retained for 180 days?
3) If Ellis requests a full data wipe, what is the process and approximate timeline (including backups/snapshots)?
4) Are there any circumstances where data could be exported outside the US (e.g., support workflows, analytics pipelines)?

Appreciate a short answer we can include in the RFP.

Thanks,
Marta
Senior Security Manager
Ellis & Co

Attachment: Ellis_Security_Questionnaire.pdf (pdf, 1 page)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Questions on hosted API data residency & purge controls

Hi Marta —

Thanks for sending the questionnaire. Below are concise answers for the Ellis procurement packet. I’ve kept them short so you can paste them into your RFP doc; Ben and Kim are looped for any technical/legal precision.

1) Storage residency: For the Redwood hosted API, customer data at rest for a given tenant is provisioned in the selected cloud region (for Ellis: us-west-2). By default we do not replicate customer request/response payloads to other regions. Replication across regions only occurs if the customer explicitly enables multi-region DR in their account settings or purchases a geo-redundant Dedicated offering.

2) Retention windows: We provide tenant-level retention controls. Typical defaults: conversational request/response payloads are retained 90 days; token-level audit logs retained 365 days. These are configurable. For Ellis we can set conversational logs to a 30-day maximum and configure audit logs to 180 days as a contractual setting on the hosted plan. Adjustments to shorter retention windows are handled via support request + configuration change and are enforced within 24 hours.

3) Full data wipe and timeline: If you request a tenant-wide purge, the flow is: (a) a vetted support/CS ticket is opened; (b) we run a coordinated deletion that zeroes active stores (primary object store and any cached KV/indices) and triggers a snapshot/backup purge job. Primary data deletion completes within 48 hours; background purge of backups and immutable snapshots completes within 30 days. We provide an attestation of deletion once the workflow completes. For higher assurance (e.g., regulatory audits) we can provide export of deletion artifacts and a sequencing report.

4) Cross-border export: We do not export customer payload data outside configured customer regions for processing. Exceptions: (i) if a customer explicitly authorizes cross-region analytics or opt-in telemetry; (ii) emergency support sessions where a limited data extract is temporarily moved for troubleshooting — these actions require documented approval and are logged. All support access is JIT (just-in-time) and audited.

See attached: redwood-data-lifecycle-summary.pdf — a short one-page map of retention vs storage. Ben/Kim — please add any nuance around encryption, backups, and attestations.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Security & Trust
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-data-lifecycle-summary.pdf (pdf, 1 page)

Marta / Grace — quick technical clarifications to supplement Grace’s note: 

- Encryption and keys: All customer payloads at rest are encrypted using AES-256. By default keys are managed by Redwood KMS (cloud-managed). For Ellis we can support customer-managed keys (CMKs) in a customer-owned KMS to ensure key material never leaves your control — this is an opt-in configuration and will be documented in the contract.

- Backups & immutable snapshots: Daily incremental backups are retained for disaster recovery. When a tenant purge is requested we mark prior backups for deletion and run an asynchronous sweep. Because cloud object stores can have retention or eventual consistency windows, final irrevocable removal from all backup layers is completed within the 30-day purge window Grace described. We provide an exportable deletion manifest when purge completes.

- Audit trails & token logs: Token-level telemetry used for billing and abuse detection is stored in a separate, tamper-evident audit system. You requested 180 days — we can set that retention and provide read-only access to retention metrics for a period defined in the SLA.

If you want us to convert any of these bullets into exact RFP language (single-paragraph answers), say which ones and we’ll produce short, copyable snippets.

—Ben
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference
